REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - OCTOBER 26, 2017 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
OCTOBER 26, 2017, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Rick Westra, Trinity Christian Reformed Church,
  Artesia.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was given by City of Cerritos Recreation Services Youth
  Football League Pee-Wee Division Team, “Seahawks.”

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido

  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu was noted absent for the record.

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  A presentation was made by:

  Los Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn ($110,000 donation to Cerritos
  Center for the Performing Arts for the Arts Education Program).

  A proclamation was presented to:

  Young Systems (Business Spotlight).

5B.  Ratification of Mayor’s Appointment to the Bellflower Unified School District
  Citizen’s Task Force

  This item was continued to the next City Council meeting.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Anantha Ramachandran requested City Council consideration of SB 415 and
  televising the Community Safety Committee meetings.

  Jennifer Pilapil commended the Council on the efficient work near Del Amo
  Boulevard. She submitted a document for the record related to City trees.

  Bonnie Sprauge expressed support for the continuation of the water aerobics
  class.
 City of Cerritos  October 26, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Mel Cortez expressed concerns with cars unloaded on Studebaker, requested
  financial support for the Neighborhood Watch program, commended the public
  safety Town Hall meeting, and requested non-political appointments to the
  Community Safety Committee.

  Murali Vasudevan commended the public safety Town Hall meeting and
  expressed concerns that Community Safety Committee members meeting
  attendance.

  Katherine George Chu requested support for the adaptive recreation game night,
  requested additional handicapped parking spaces at Sprouts, and thanked those
  that supported the Tip-A-Cop fundraiser for Special Olympics at Wood Ranch
  Restaurant.

  Paul Gupta expressed concerns regarding traffic safety near the Emerald Villas
  senior housing development and requested traffic signal adjustment.

  Nestor Roldan expressed concerns regarding traffic safety near the Emerald
  Villas senior housing development and requested traffic signal adjustment.

  John Watts expressed concerns with City-wide tree maintenance.

  Sam Desai spoke regarding his business center project and requested City
  Council appoint a resident to its Board of Directors, commended residents for
  their community service, and expressed concerns regarding obtaining a City
  business license.

  Paul Bellenbaum referred to articles written in a local community newspaper and
  suggested an amendment to the State Constitution regarding eligibility to run
  for elected office in California.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of
  October 9, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of October 9, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (4 – 0, Hu absent) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Hu
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 26, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of Registers of Demands

  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated October 26, 2017
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Registers of Demands as follows:

  1. City of Cerritos  10/26/2017 $2,304,211.20 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (4 – 0, Hu absent) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Hu
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration by the Cerritos City Council to enter into a five (5) year
  lease agreement with Southern California Edison, and concurrent five (5) year
  sublease agreements with various Cerritos Auto Square dealers, to continue the
  existing use of two (2) Southern California Edison-owned properties for Cerritos
  Auto Square vehicle storage purposes. The first property, the Studebaker Road
  facility, is generally located south of 183rd Street, east of the San Gabriel River
  Channel, and north of South Street (APNS 7038-011-800, 7038-011-801, 7038-
  012-800, 7038-012-802). The second property, the Del Amo Boulevard facility, is
  generally located east of Studebaker Road, north of Del Amo Boulevard, and west
  of State Road (APNS 7049-021-804, 7049-021-805) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor Pro Tem opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke in opposition to the approval of lease agreements
  citing the number of sublicense agreements, attorney costs, and the need for
  additional information.

  Murali Vasudevan spoke in opposition to the approval of lease agreements citing
  concern with the City acting as property manager.

  Mel Cortez spoke in opposition to the approval of lease agreements citing while
  the Auto Mall is good for the economic health of the City, we do not have
  evidence Edison will not deal with private property owners.

  Sam Desai spoke in opposition to the approval of lease agreements citing
  inappropriate subsidies and last minute disclosures.

  Scott Smith, Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce, spoke in support of the
  lease agreements as the Auto Mall is a major economic driver for the City.

  Noting there were no further members of the public who elected to speak, the
  Mayor Pro Tem closed public comments and the public hearing.
 City of Cerritos  October 26, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 8

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to authorize the City
  Manager, or his designee, to execute the master license agreements between the
  City of Cerritos and Southern California Edison, and subsequent sublicense
  agreements between the City of Cerritos and participating dealers, in such form
  approved by the City Manager and the City Attorney, for the use of the Edison-
  owned Studebaker Storage Facility and the Del Amo Storage Facility (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0, Hu absent) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Hu
  ABSTAIN:  None

8B.  Review and consideration of a request to sell the five (5) acre City-owned parcel
  located east of the San Gabriel River Channel, west of Dumont Avenue between
  183rd Street and Artesia Boulevard (APN 7034-018-901) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherre Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor Pro Tem opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Mary Buell, applicant, spoke in support of sale of the property to the Buell family
  and provide a history of the property.

  Barry Rabbitt spoke in support of sale of the property to the Buell family.

  Mickey Brooks spoke in support of sale of the property to the Buell family.

  Brenda Trimble spoke in support of sale of the property to the Buell family.

  Murali Vasudevan spoke in opposition to the sale of the property to the Buell
  family.

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke in opposition to the sale of the property to the
  Buell family.

  Mel Cortez spoke in opposition to the sale of the property to the Buell family.

  Mary Buell, applicant, provided rebuttal comments citing the therapeutic riding
  program and other community benefits of the stable.

  Noting there were no further members of the public who elected to speak, the
  Mayor Pro Tem closed public comments and the public hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to entertain the sale of
  the five (5) acre City-owned parcel located east of the San Gabriel River Channel,
  west of Dumont Avenue between 183rd Street and Artesia Boulevard (APN 7034-
  018-901) by ordering an appraisal of the subject property (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  October 26, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 8

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8B.  (continued)

  The motion did not carry (2 - 2, Hu absent) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki
  NOES:  Yokoyama, Pulido
  ABSENT:  Hu
  ABSTAIN:  None

  No further action was taken on this item.
